# ux.sgit.ai: UX, measured

> Where the sgit.ai sites fail their readers, measured on the live site, and what fixes it. A register of UX failures and gaps across the sgit.ai sites, each measured on the
> live site with a date and version, the principle it breaks, the fix, and (where one exists) a working
> prototype of the fix in three design directions.

Site version: v0.1.0 (2026-10-18). Content CC BY 4.0. Code Apache 2.0. Author: Dinis Cruz, with AI co-authorship.

## The headline

55 findings across 3 sites: 49 still open, 12 of them high severity, 6 fixed. 36 are failures (something works against the reader) and 19 are gaps (something the reader needs is not there). Every count on this site is generated from /data/findings.json.

## Properties agents may rely on

- /data/findings.json is the register. Every finding page, list, filter and count is generated from it at build, and the gate fails if a page is stale.
- Every finding has a stable page at /findings/<ID>.html and a markdown twin at /findings/<ID>.md.
- Every page has a markdown twin: replace .html with .md, or append index.md to a directory URL.
- /findings/?site=&area=&severity=&status=&kind=&principle=&q= is a linkable filter (comma-separate values for OR).
- Statuses carry the date and version they were last checked. Nothing here claims to be current beyond that date.
- /llms-full.txt is the whole site in one fetch.

## The pages

/about/  (/about/index.md)
  Who writes ux.sgit.ai, why the register is public, what it is not, and the licences.
/admin/  (/admin/index.md)
  How ux.sgit.ai is built and checked: the source files, the build, the gate, and what CI enforces.
/admin/versions.html  (/admin/versions.md)
  The release history of ux.sgit.ai: each version, its date, what it changed and the files it touched.
/findings/  (/findings/index.md)
  The register: every UX failure and gap found on the sgit.ai sites, with status, severity, the principle it breaks and the fix. Filterable, and every filter is a link.
/  (/index.md)
  A register of where the sgit.ai sites fail their readers, measured on the live site with a date and a version, the principle each failure breaks, the fix, and a working prototype of it.
/lab/  (/lab/index.md)
  Four encrypted vaults that try the newsroom review's fixes as working prototypes, on the real newsroom data, in three design directions each, before anything changes on the live site.
/method/  (/method/index.md)
  How a UX finding is made here: the reader's path, the stranger test, the review panel, what severity and status mean, and how to file a finding in the register.
/principles/  (/principles/index.md)
  The rules the findings break, each with why it matters, a one-minute test you can run on any page, and the findings that break it.
/reviews/  (/reviews/index.md)
  The full UX reviews the findings come from, published whole, with their date, the version reviewed and the method.
/reviews/newsroom-2026-10-11.html  (/reviews/newsroom-2026-10-11.md)
  The UX review of newsroom.sgit.ai (v0.6.4, re-checked on v0.7.1) that seeded this site's register: first visit, findability, the article and its feedback, personas, reader primitives, the publishing pipeline and a roadmap.

/about/  ·  /about/index.md
==============================================================================

# Why this exists

The sgit.ai sites are written in the open by Dinis Cruz with teams of AI agents, and they move fast: the newsroom shipped 73 articles in eight weeks. The content is strong. The way a stranger gets into it often is not, because the people who build a site are the last people able to see it as a stranger does.

This site is where that gets written down. Publicly, because a failure stated in the open gets fixed, and because the patterns repeat: an unlabelled number, a filter you cannot share, a rating that starts preselected. Anyone building a site, ours or not, can use the [principles](/principles/index.md) and their one-minute tests.

## Who writes it

Dinis Cruz, with AI co-authorship. Reviews are run by agents playing named roles (architect, librarian, historian, designer, editor, journalist) against measured evidence, and checked by a person. Findings come from those reviews and from anyone who uses the sites and tells us where they got stuck.

## Disclosure

Every site reviewed here is ours. The sgit.ai sites argue for sgit (encrypted git for humans and agents) and RiskMandate (behaviour policies for agents), and the author builds both. This site has an interest in those sites working, which is the reason it exists, and no interest in hiding where they do not.

## What this is not

- **Not a style guide.** How code is written is [coding.sgit.ai](https://coding.sgit.ai/). This is what the reader experiences.
- **Not a live monitor.** Every status is dated. Nothing here claims to be current beyond the date it was checked.
- **Not a scorecard of people.** A finding is about a page and a reader, never about who built it.

## Licences

Content CC BY 4.0: take it, adapt it, build on it, with attribution. Code Apache 2.0. The newsroom review quotes and measures newsroom.sgit.ai, which is also CC BY 4.0.


==============================================================================
/admin/  ·  /admin/index.md
==============================================================================

# How it is built

A static site, generated by a small Python build with no dependencies, served as plain files. No framework, no client-side rendering: every page is complete HTML before any script runs, and the one script on the site (the findings filter) only hides and shows rows that are already there.

## The files

| Path | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `data/findings.json` | The register. The source of every finding page, list, filter and count |
| `data/principles.json` | The principles, each with a rule, a reason and a test |
| `data/lab.json` | The design lab: vaults and read keys, directions, screenshots, decisions |
| `data/site.json` | Name, navigation, the sites reviewed, the sibling sites |
| `data/versions.json` | The release history; the first entry is the current version |
| `content/**/*.md` | Hand-written pages, with `{{directives}}` the build fills from the data |
| `admin/build/build.py` | Builds every `.html`, its `.md` twin, `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt`, `sitemap.xml` |
| `admin/build/md.py` | The markdown renderer (stdlib only) |
| `admin/build/gate.py` | The release gate |
| `assets/` | One stylesheet, one script, the icon |
| `lab/shots/` | Phone screenshots from the lab's vaults |

## Build and check

```
python3 admin/build/build.py     # write every generated file
python3 admin/build/gate.py      # must print GATE PASS
python3 -m http.server 8000      # then open http://localhost:8000/
```

## The gate

CI runs it on every push, and a release is the commit it passes on. It fails if:

- any generated file is stale (the build is re-run and compared byte for byte), or any `.html` in the tree is not generated;
- a finding is missing a field, uses an unknown site, area, kind, severity, status or principle, repeats an id, or has a date that is not a date;
- a principle has no finding that breaks it;
- an internal link or `#anchor` on any page goes nowhere, or a page has no markdown twin;
- a colour is written anywhere but the token block at the top of `assets/site.css`;
- the version disagrees between `data/versions.json`, the pages, `llms.txt` and `index.md`;
- a lab screenshot named in `data/lab.json` is missing, or a credential that is not a published read key appears in a tracked file.

## Versions

The version is shown once, in the footer, and links to [what changed](/admin/versions.md).

# Versions

The current version is v0.1.0. Newest first.

## v0.1.0 · 2026-10-18

The first release: a register of UX failures and gaps, seeded from the newsroom review, with the review, the design lab and the method it was made by.

- `data/findings.json`: 55 findings (newsroom.sgit.ai, the vault host, and the lab's own prototypes), each with evidence, impact, fix, status and the principle it breaks
- `data/principles.json`: 14 principles, each listing the findings that break it
- `content/reviews/newsroom-2026-10-11.md`: the newsroom UX review of 11 October 2026, published whole
- `content/lab/index.md + lab/shots/`: the Newsroom Design Lab, its four vaults with read keys, and 24 phone screenshots in three directions
- `content/method/index.md`: the reader path, the panel, severity, and how a finding is filed
- `admin/build/`: build.py, md.py and gate.py, stdlib only

[Findings](/findings/index.md) / UX-001

# The first phone screen explains how the site is built, not what it is about

Open · high severity · failure · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

At 390×844 the first screen holds a two-row header, a "For agents /llms.txt" strip, three lines of metadata, a tagline about method, a second navigation bar and an editor's note. The lead story starts on screen two.

## Why it matters

A contact who taps a link cannot tell in one screen that this is a publication about AI agents, security and publishing, or why they were sent it.

## The fix

One sentence on what this is, who writes it, three doors (security, builders, news) and the lead, all on screen one. Everything else moves below or into the menu.

## The record

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Status** | Open |
| **Severity** | High |
| **Kind** | Failure: works against the reader |
| **Site** | [newsroom.sgit.ai](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/) |
| **Where** | <https://newsroom.sgit.ai/> |
| **Area** | [First visit](/findings/?area=first-visit) |
| **Breaks** | [The first screen is for a stranger](/principles/index.md#stranger-first-screen) |
| **Observed** | 2026-10-11, v0.6.4 |
| **Last checked** | 2026-10-11, v0.7.1 |
| **Source** | [Review: first visit](/reviews/newsroom-2026-10-11.md#first-visit-a-contact-arriving-from-a-link) |
| **Prototype** | [Front page & personas](/lab/index.md#newsroom-proto-front), route `first-screen`, in three directions |

[Findings](/findings/index.md) / UX-002

# The home page is 59 phone screens long, with 845 links

Open · high severity · failure · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

The phone home page measures 49,715 px: Latest, Highlights, desk notes, collections, the full article list, then a map of every article's links.

## Why it matters

The front page tries to show everything, so it chooses nothing for the reader. Nobody scrolls 59 screens; the curation is invisible.

## The fix

Cut the home page to the lead, three per desk, collections and the newsletter. Lists and the link map move to their own pages.

## The record

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Status** | Open |
| **Severity** | High |
| **Kind** | Failure: works against the reader |
| **Site** | [newsroom.sgit.ai](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/) |

[Findings](/findings/index.md) / UX-003

# The masthead line describes a method, not a subject

Open · medium severity · gap · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

The tagline is "one page, one argument, with the figures, the data and the links to check it". Nothing says agents, AI governance, security or news economics.

## Why it matters

The one line every visitor reads tells them how the site works instead of what it is about.

## The fix

A masthead line that names the subject and the author, e.g. "Field notes on AI agents, security and the next generation of publishing, by Dinis Cruz".

## The record

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Status** | Open |
| **Severity** | Medium |
| **Kind** | Gap: something the reader needs is not there |
| **Site** | [newsroom.sgit.ai](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/) |
| **Where** | <https://newsroom.sgit.ai/> |

[Findings](/findings/index.md) / UX-004

# The edition label is older than the articles under it

Open · medium severity · failure · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

The home page says "Edition of 2026-10-08" above ten articles dated 10 October. Still the case in v0.7.1, above articles from 10 and 11 October.

## Why it matters

A front page that looks three days stale on the day it was published tells a reader the site is not kept.

## The fix

Date the edition from the newest article at build time, or label it as the editor's pick of its date.

## The record

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Status** | Open |
| **Severity** | Medium |
| **Kind** | Failure: works against the reader |
| **Site** | [newsroom.sgit.ai](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/) |
| **Where** | <https://newsroom.sgit.ai/> |
| **Area** | [First visit](/findings/?area=first-visit) |
| **Breaks** | [What a page says about the present is true now](/principles/index.md#state-is-current) |
| **Observed** | 2026-10-11, v0.6.4 |
| **Last checked** | 2026-10-11, v0.7.1 |
| **Source** | [Review: bugs and broken things](/reviews/newsroom-2026-10-11.md#bugs-and-broken-things) |

# The version number is shown three times on the first screen

Open · low severity · failure · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

v0.7.1 appears three times on the desktop first screen: in the agent strip, the metadata lines and the footer badge.

## Why it matters

Engineering detail repeated where a reader looks first; it reads as a demo, not a publication.

## The fix

One version, in the workshop and the page foot, linked to what changed. None on the reader's first screen.

## The record

[Findings](/findings/index.md) / UX-006

# A "For agents /llms.txt" strip sits above the masthead

Open · low severity · failure · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

The first element on every page is a strip addressed to agents, above the publication's name.

## Why it matters

Useful to agents, noise to a person, and it takes the most valuable line on the screen.

## The fix

Move it to the page head (link rel) and the footer, where agents look anyway. Satisfies both the Architect and the Designer on the panel.

## The record

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Status** | Open |
| **Severity** | Low |
| **Kind** | Failure: works against the reader |

| **Area** | [First visit](/findings/?area=first-visit) |

[Findings](/findings/index.md) / UX-007

# The editor's note is written for someone who read the last two editions

Open · low severity · failure · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

The note opens "Third edition... the last two days", assuming the reader has followed along.

## Why it matters

The one personal voice on the front page talks past the newcomer the page most needs to win.

## The fix

Write the note for a newcomer: what this edition is about and where to start.

## The record

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Status** | Open |
| **Severity** | Low |
| **Kind** | Failure: works against the reader |
| **Site** | [newsroom.sgit.ai](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/) |
| **Where** | <https://newsroom.sgit.ai/> |
| **Area** | [First visit](/findings/?area=first-visit) |
| **Breaks** | [The first screen is for a stranger](/principles/index.md#stranger-first-screen) |
| **Observed** | 2026-10-11, v0.6.4 |

[Findings](/findings/index.md) / UX-008

# Content is hidden until JavaScript runs

Open · medium severity · failure · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

The body starts at opacity 0 and only appears when a "ready" class is added, with a 1.6 s fallback.

## Why it matters

On a slow phone, or for any reader or agent that does not run the script, the page is blank.

## The fix

Render visible by default; animate only enhancements.

## The record

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Status** | Open |
| **Severity** | Medium |
| **Kind** | Failure: works against the reader |
| **Site** | [newsroom.sgit.ai](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/) |

| **Area** | [Trust](/findings/?area=trust) |

| **Observed** | 2026-10-11, v0.6.4 |
| **Last checked** | 2026-10-11, v0.7.1 |
| **Source** | [Review: bugs and broken things](/reviews/newsroom-2026-10-11.md#bugs-and-broken-things) |

[Findings](/findings/index.md) / UX-009

# Two navigation bars, and a 60-link menu that mixes reading with building

Open · medium severity · failure · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

A second bar of nine links repeats the menu. The menu holds about 60 links in nine groups (57 links in 8 groups when the lab mapped it), mixing reader pages (Newsletter, Collections) with builder pages (Replicate, Admin, Release history, The run log).

## Why it matters

The reader has to sort the publication from the workshop themselves, twice.

## The fix

One navigation. The publication on top; the workshop behind one item with its own front page.

## The record

# Missing pages show the default GitHub Pages 404

Open · medium severity · failure · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

Any missing URL shows GitHub's generic error page, with no link back to the newsroom.

# Links without extensions in one article

Open · low severity · failure · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

future-of-news links to /thesis, /portugal and /economics/rails, unlike every other link on the site.

## Why it matters

They depend on the host resolving extensionless paths; on a strict host or a mirror they break.

## The fix

Use the full .html or trailing-slash form everywhere; check it at build.

# Each article ends with seven next steps instead of one

Open · low severity · failure · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

After the rating scales the foot of an article offers many routes onward with equal weight.

## Why it matters

At the moment the reader is most ready to continue, the page makes them choose among seven.

## The fix

One next step: the next part of the series, or the next "start here" piece for the reader's desk, then the newsletter.

[Findings](/findings/index.md) / UX-013

# One topic holds more than half the articles

Open · medium severity · failure · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

"Agents & policy" holds 35 of 67 articles (38 of 73 in the lab's snapshot). The other five topics hold 13 to 26 and overlap: an article sits in about two.

## Why it matters

A CISO who picks the obvious topic still faces 35 long reads. The classification does not help anyone choose.

## The fix

Desks by audience, not internal topic: security, building, vaults, news, strategy (18 / 17 / 14 / 15 / 9 in the lab).

## The record

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Status** | Open |
| **Severity** | Medium |

| **Last checked** | 2026-10-11, v0.7.1 |

[Findings](/findings/index.md) / UX-014

# Tags are not links, and there are no tag pages

Open · medium severity · failure · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

The lead article carries 12 tag pills; none links anywhere. Tags mix subjects, formats and product names ("article", "riskmandate"). 339 raw tags, 228 used once.

## Why it matters

The most precise way into the archive looks clickable and goes nowhere.

## The fix

A controlled vocabulary of about 40 tags owned by the Librarian, a page per tag, tags as links capped at five per article (339 → 42 in the lab; median 11 → 4).

## The record

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Status** | Open |
| **Severity** | Medium |
| **Kind** | Failure: works against the reader |

| **Last checked** | 2026-10-11, v0.7.1 |

[Findings](/findings/index.md) / UX-015

# Filters cannot be shared

Open · medium severity · gap · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

Choosing a topic on the article list does not change the address.

## Why it matters

You cannot send a contact "the security articles"; you can only send the whole list and an instruction.

## The fix

Put every filter in the address (/articles/?desk=security, or in the path where query strings are not allowed).

## The record

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Status** | Open |
| **Severity** | Medium |

[Findings](/findings/index.md) / UX-016

# Series are invisible

Open · medium severity · gap · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

The reading meter in five pieces, the homepage diagnosis and its rebuild, the agent team in three depths: nothing says "part 2 of 5" or offers the next part. The lab found eleven series.

## Why it matters

Readers land in the middle of a story without knowing there is a beginning.

## The fix

Series pages with part numbers, previous / next on each part, and the reader's progress.

## The record

# There is no "start here" path

Open · medium severity · gap · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

The Historian's weekly note and the collections are the best orientation on the site, and they sit below the fold.

## Why it matters

Each desk opens with "Start here: five articles in order", written by the Historian.

# Cards do not show reading time or format

Open · medium severity · gap · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

The median article is about 4,500 words and 25 of 66 are over 5,000, yet no card shows reading time or whether it is a field report, explainer, analysis or desk note.

## Why it matters

A reader with three minutes cannot tell a note from a 40-minute analysis before opening it.

## The fix

Reading time and a format label on every card, derived at build.

# Search only matches titles, teasers and tags

## What we saw

The search box does not look inside articles, although a markdown twin of every article exists.

[Findings](/findings/index.md) / UX-020

# The best reader feature is buried under metadata and a long italic abstract

Open · medium severity · failure · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

On the lead article (about 8,000 words) a phone reader scrolls past a three-line breadcrumb, a byline with two version numbers, 12 tag pills and a 250-word italic abstract before reaching the "Five readers" block.

## Why it matters

The short version that would let a reader decide is found only by those who already decided to read.

## The fix

Title and standfirst; a byline that says how it was made, date and reading time; the short version in three or four sentences; reader views as one row; then the article. Tags and versions to the foot.

## The record

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Status** | Open |
| **Severity** | Medium |
| **Kind** | Failure: works against the reader |
| **Site** | [newsroom.sgit.ai](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/) |
| **Where** | <https://newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/hope-or-enforcement.html> |
| **Area** | [Article page](/findings/?area=article) |
| **Breaks** | [Say how long, and what kind, before the reader commits](/principles/index.md#length-before-commitment) |
| **Observed** | 2026-10-11, v0.6.4 |
| **Last checked** | 2026-10-11, v0.7.1 |
| **Source** | [Review: article page and feedback](/reviews/newsroom-2026-10-11.md#article-page-and-feedback) |
| **Prototype** | [Article & reader primitives](/lab/index.md#newsroom-proto-article), route `article/hope-or-enforcement`, in three directions |

# The byline names one human; the AI authorship is in the footer

Open · medium severity · failure · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

Articles are written from voice notes by a desk of named agents; the byline says only "Dinis Cruz" and the agent newsroom is credited in the footer.

A reader who finds the disclosure late reads it as something hidden, on a publication whose pitch is provenance.

"Dinis Cruz, written with the SGit agent newsroom" in the byline, linked to the purpose page.

[Findings](/findings/index.md) / UX-023

# There is no page that says why the publication exists

Open · medium severity · gap · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

The agenda (build sgit.ai and RiskMandate, which most articles use as evidence), the licences and the participant disclosure are spread across the footer and method pages.

## Why it matters

Readers cannot judge the argument without knowing who is making it and why.

## The fix

A purpose page, linked from the masthead and every byline: the agenda, open by default, how it is written, who it is for, what I want from you.

## The record

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Status** | Open |
| **Severity** | Medium |
| **Kind** | Gap: something the reader needs is not there |
| **Site** | [newsroom.sgit.ai](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/) |
| **Where** | <https://newsroom.sgit.ai/> |
| **Area** | [Trust](/findings/?area=trust) |
| **Breaks** | [Say who wrote it, and how](/principles/index.md#say-who-wrote-it) |
| **Observed** | 2026-10-11, v0.6.4 |
| **Last checked** | 2026-10-11, v0.7.1 |
| **Source** | [Review: the direction](/reviews/newsroom-2026-10-11.md#the-direction-a-publication-with-a-heart) |
| **Prototype** | [Front page & personas](/lab/index.md#newsroom-proto-front), route `purpose`, in three directions |

[Findings](/findings/index.md) / UX-024

# All three rating scales start on 3

Open · high severity · failure · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

The usefulness, more-like-this and level-of-detail scales at the foot of every article are preselected on the middle value.

## Why it matters

Neither the reader nor the author can tell "not rated" from "useful". Every rating collected so far is ambiguous.

## The fix

Start unselected; record only real taps.

## The record

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Status** | Open |
| **Severity** | High |
| **Kind** | Failure: works against the reader |
| **Site** | [newsroom.sgit.ai](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/) |
| **Where** | <https://newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/> |
| **Area** | [Feedback](/findings/?area=feedback) |
| **Breaks** | [A default is not an answer](/principles/index.md#defaults-are-not-answers) |
| **Observed** | 2026-10-11, v0.6.4 |
| **Last checked** | 2026-10-11, v0.7.1 |
| **Source** | [Review: article page and feedback](/reviews/newsroom-2026-10-11.md#article-page-and-feedback) |
| **Prototype** | [Article & reader primitives](/lab/index.md#newsroom-proto-article), route `feedback`, in three directions |

Previous: [UX-023 There is no page that says why the publication exists](/findings/UX-023.md)

Next: [UX-025 Ratings never reach the author](/findings/UX-025.md)

[Findings](/findings/index.md) / UX-025

# Ratings never reach the author

Open · high severity · gap · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

Ratings stay in the reader's browser unless they choose to send their whole reading record.

## Why it matters

The first contacts sent to the site teach the author nothing about what landed.

## The fix

One-tap send by default, with plain consent ("Send this rating to Dinis, anonymous"), through the encrypted append lane, with a local receipt.

## The record

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Status** | Open |
| **Severity** | High |
| **Kind** | Gap: something the reader needs is not there |
| **Site** | [newsroom.sgit.ai](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/) |
| **Where** | <https://newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/> |
| **Area** | [Feedback](/findings/?area=feedback) |
| **Breaks** | [Feedback reaches someone, and the reader gets a receipt](/principles/index.md#feedback-reaches-someone) |
| **Observed** | 2026-10-11, v0.6.4 |
| **Last checked** | 2026-10-11, v0.7.1 |
| **Source** | [Review: article page and feedback](/reviews/newsroom-2026-10-11.md#article-page-and-feedback) |
| **Prototype** | [Article & reader primitives](/lab/index.md#newsroom-proto-article), route `feedback`, in three directions |

[Findings](/findings/index.md) / UX-026

# There is no way to say what was missing

Open · low severity · gap · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

Feedback is three scales and nothing else: no free text, no "write about this", no "I need a new version".

## Why it matters

Scores say what, not why. Requests that would become the next pitches have no channel.

## The fix

One optional line ("What would have made this more useful?") and request buttons, sent through the append lane with a receipt.

## The record

[Findings](/findings/index.md) / UX-027

# Articles join the reader's list without being asked

Open · medium severity · failure · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

Opening an article adds it to the reader's reading list automatically.

## Why it matters

The list stops meaning "what I chose to keep" and becomes a history the reader did not ask for.

## The fix

Make "Keep" a tap.

[Findings](/findings/index.md) / UX-028

# The £5.00 balance chip has no label

Open · high severity · failure · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

An unlabelled "£5.00" sits in the header of every page. Still unlabelled in v0.7.1.

## Why it matters

An amount of money with no explanation reads as a bill or a trap; the synthetic-user study flagged it.

## The fix

Label it "£5 free reading credit".

## The record

[Findings](/findings/index.md) / UX-029

# Opening an article charges a penny with no notice

Open · high severity · failure · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

The chip changes from £5.00 to £4.99 on opening any article, silently. In the synthetic-user study this exact moment made a retired reader ask whether she owed money.

## Why it matters

The first thing a new reader learns about the reading meter is that their balance dropped without being told.

## The fix

Announce the first charge once, in words, at the moment it happens.

## The record

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Status** | Open |
| **Severity** | High |
| **Kind** | Failure: works against the reader |
| **Site** | [newsroom.sgit.ai](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/) |
| **Where** | <https://newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/> |
| **Area** | [Money](/findings/?area=money) |
| **Breaks** | [Label the money, and never surprise with a charge](/principles/index.md#label-the-money) |
| **Observed** | 2026-10-11, v0.6.4 |
| **Last checked** | 2026-10-11, v0.7.1 |
| **Source** | [Review: first visit](/reviews/newsroom-2026-10-11.md#first-visit-a-contact-arriving-from-a-link) |

# "You pay the price" reads as a warning

Open · low severity · failure · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

The caption under the usefulness scale reads "You pay the price".

"Your rating sets what this page costs you".

# It is unclear how a writer gets paid

Open · high severity · gap · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

The site states nothing is paid upstream yet, and does not say what will be. A blocking finding of the synthetic-user study.

## Why it matters

Writers and publishers, the people the meter is pitched to, cannot see where their share comes from.

## The fix

Say plainly what is paid today (nothing), what is planned and when.

# No contact for a pilot on the Replicate page

Open · high severity · gap · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

The page that invites publishers to replicate the newsroom has no name, email or form.

The one reader ready to act has nowhere to go. A blocking finding of the synthetic-user study.

[Findings](/findings/index.md) / UX-035

# The top-up page said "simulated" while asking for money

Fixed · high severity · failure · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

The synthetic-user run of 10 October found the top-up page asking for a payment while describing itself as simulated.

## Why it matters

A payment page that says it is not real is a payment page nobody can trust.

## The fix

Describe the one real Stripe payment. Done in v0.6.4; real Stripe top-up live since 11 October.

## The record

[Findings](/findings/index.md) / UX-036

# Articles were published on two domains, and diverged

Fixed · high severity · failure · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

sgit.ai/articles/ served five 11 October articles (e.g. no-server-by-design, the-agent-is-the-reader) that returned 404 on newsroom.sgit.ai.

## Why it matters

The same publication was more complete on the wrong site.

## The fix

Publish once to the newsroom; make sgit.ai link or redirect there.

## The record

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Status** | Fixed. Fixed in v0.7.1: all six 11 October articles are live on the newsroom; the count is 73. |
| **Severity** | High |
| **Kind** | Failure: works against the reader |
| **Site** | [newsroom.sgit.ai](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/) |
| **Where** | <https://sgit.ai/articles/> |
| **Area** | [Consistency](/findings/?area=consistency) |
| **Breaks** | [One source of truth for every fact](/principles/index.md#one-source-of-truth) |

[Findings](/findings/index.md) / UX-037

# Two domains claim to be canonical for the same article

Open · high severity · failure · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

sgit.ai/articles/hope-or-enforcement.html declares canonical sgit.ai; the newsroom copy declares canonical newsroom.sgit.ai.

## Why it matters

Search engines split the article's standing between two copies, and readers can land on either.

## The fix

One canonical, the newsroom; a 301 or a canonical pointing there from sgit.ai.

## The record

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Status** | Open |
| **Severity** | High |
| **Kind** | Failure: works against the reader |
| **Site** | [newsroom.sgit.ai](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/) |
| **Where** | <https://sgit.ai/articles/hope-or-enforcement.html> |
| **Area** | [Consistency](/findings/?area=consistency) |
| **Breaks** | [One source of truth for every fact](/principles/index.md#one-source-of-truth) |
| **Observed** | 2026-10-11, v0.6.4 |
| **Last checked** | 2026-10-11, v0.7.1 |
| **Source** | [Review: bugs and broken things](/reviews/newsroom-2026-10-11.md#bugs-and-broken-things) |

[Findings](/findings/index.md) / UX-038

# Three different article counts

Open · medium severity · failure · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

sgit.ai said 72, the newsroom home said 67, llms.txt said 66, on the same day.

## Why it matters

When a site cannot count itself, the reader doubts every other number on it.

## The fix

Generate every count from one manifest at build, and fail the release if any page disagrees.

## The record

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Status** | Open. wire.json says 73 in v0.7.1; the three surfaces were not re-compared. |
| **Severity** | Medium |
| **Kind** | Failure: works against the reader |

| **Where** | <https://newsroom.sgit.ai/> |

| **Last checked** | 2026-10-11, v0.7.1 |

[Findings](/findings/index.md) / UX-041

# 51 vault images missing across 10 articles

Fixed · high severity · failure · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

The third synthetic-user run found 51 vault images returning 404 in 10 articles.

## Why it matters

Evidence images are the point of an evidence-first article; broken ones undo the claim.

## The fix

Fixed: 0 broken images on 10 rendered articles in v0.6.4.

## The record

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Status** | Fixed. Fixed by v0.6.4. |
| **Severity** | High |
| **Kind** | Failure: works against the reader |
| **Site** | [newsroom.sgit.ai](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/) |
| **Where** | <https://newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/> |
| **Area** | [Consistency](/findings/?area=consistency) |
| **Breaks** | [No dead ends](/principles/index.md#no-dead-ends) |
| **Observed** | 2026-10-10, v0.6.1 |
| **Last checked** | 2026-10-11, v0.6.4 |
| **Source** | [Review: synthetic users](/reviews/newsroom-2026-10-11.md#synthetic-users-what-is-fixed-and-what-is-open) |

# Persona pages are a list, with no story, opinion or next step

## What we saw

[Findings](/findings/index.md) / UX-046

# Setting location.hash inside a vault app re-navigates the frame: every link silently dead

Open · high severity · failure · dev.vault.sgraph.ai

## What we saw

In the host the app is an about:srcdoc frame, where assigning location.hash re-navigates instead of firing hashchange. The How Much Evidence vault shipped on 5 October 2026 with every view link dead.

## Why it matters

An app that works when opened as a file ships to readers with no working navigation, and nothing errors.

## The fix

Keep the route in a variable; catch a[href^="#"] in a capture click handler; mark links data-sg-native; use the hash only when running standalone. Documented in the sgit.ai guidance.

## The record

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Status** | Open. Open as a platform trap; every lab vault avoids it. |
| **Severity** | High |
| **Kind** | Failure: works against the reader |
| **Site** | [dev.vault.sgraph.ai](https://dev.vault.sgraph.ai/) |
| **Where** | any vault app that routes by hash |
| **Area** | [Platform](/findings/?area=platform) |
| **Breaks** | [A vault app works inside the host, not just on its own](/principles/index.md#host-safe-apps) |
| **Observed** | 2026-10-05, host |
| **Last checked** | 2026-10-11, host |
| **Source** | [Design lab: what building it measured](/lab/index.md#what-building-the-lab-measured) |

Previous: [UX-045 Persona pages are a list, with no story, opinion or next step](/findings/UX-045.md)

Next: [UX-047 localStorage throws inside the vault app frame, so reader data is lost on reload](/findings/UX-047.md)

[Findings](/findings/index.md) / UX-047

# localStorage throws inside the vault app frame, so reader data is lost on reload

Open · medium severity · failure · dev.vault.sgraph.ai

## What we saw

The app frame refuses localStorage with SecurityError. Lab kit v0.1.2 kept highlights, notes and ratings only until reload.

## Why it matters

A reader's notes disappear on reload, the worst failure a note-taking feature can have.

## The fix

Store through the host's async sg.state (survives reload). Kit v0.1.3 does; every lab vault was republished on it.

## The record

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Status** | Open. Open as a platform trap; fixed in the lab by kit v0.1.3. |
| **Severity** | Medium |
| **Kind** | Failure: works against the reader |
| **Site** | [dev.vault.sgraph.ai](https://dev.vault.sgraph.ai/) |
| **Where** | any vault app that stores reader state |
| **Area** | [Platform](/findings/?area=platform) |
| **Breaks** | [A vault app works inside the host, not just on its own](/principles/index.md#host-safe-apps) |
| **Observed** | 2026-10-11, host |
| **Last checked** | 2026-10-11, host |
| **Source** | [Design lab: what building it measured](/lab/index.md#what-building-the-lab-measured) |

Previous: [UX-046 Setting location.hash inside a vault app re-navigates the frame: every link silently dead](/findings/UX-046.md)

[Findings](/findings/index.md) / UX-048

# A vault app can load images and scripts from a site but cannot fetch its data

Open · low severity · gap · dev.vault.sgraph.ai

## What we saw

The host CSP is connect-src blob: data:. fetch() to newsroom.sgit.ai is refused although it sends access-control-allow-origin *, while <img> and classic <script src> from the same origin load.

## Why it matters

Builders reasonably expect CORS-open data to be readable and discover otherwise in production; apps must snapshot data instead.

## The fix

Snapshot the data into the vault (with SHA-256 in sources.json) and say in the UI which copy is shown. State the CSP where builders read about vault apps.

## The record

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Status** | Open |
| **Severity** | Low |
| **Kind** | Gap: something the reader needs is not there |
| **Site** | [dev.vault.sgraph.ai](https://dev.vault.sgraph.ai/) |
| **Where** | vault apps reading newsroom.sgit.ai |
| **Area** | [Platform](/findings/?area=platform) |
| **Breaks** | [A vault app works inside the host, not just on its own](/principles/index.md#host-safe-apps) |
| **Observed** | 2026-10-11, host |
| **Last checked** | 2026-10-11, host |
| **Source** | [Design lab: what building it measured](/lab/index.md#what-building-the-lab-measured) |

Previous: [UX-047 localStorage throws inside the vault app frame, so reader data is lost on reload](/findings/UX-047.md)

[Findings](/findings/index.md) / UX-049

# Query strings break inside the vault host, so filters must live in the route path

Open · low severity · gap · dev.vault.sgraph.ai

## What we saw

Adding a query string to an app route breaks in the srcdoc frame.

## Why it matters

The usual way to make a filter linkable is not available; each app has to invent a path encoding.

## The fix

Encode filters in the path in a fixed order (desk, format, tag, series, month, q), as the findability vault does.

## The record

| **Area** | [Platform](/findings/?area=platform) |

[Findings](/findings/index.md) / UX-050

# File-path pills scrolled the whole page sideways at 390 px

Fixed · medium severity · failure · newsroom-design-lab

## What we saw

Long, unbreakable file-path pills on the data pages pushed the page wider than a phone.

## Why it matters

Sideways scroll on a phone makes every line harder to read and hides the edge of the content.

## The fix

Let pills wrap; the gate now fails on any sideways scroll at 390 px. Fixed in kit v0.1.2.

## The record

# Re-rendering the whole view on every save lost the reader's place

Fixed · medium severity · failure · newsroom-design-lab

## What we saw

Every store write (a highlight, a note, a status) re-rendered the whole reading view and jumped the scroll position.

## Why it matters

A reader who highlights a sentence is thrown somewhere else in an 8,000-word article.

## The fix

Repaint only the parts that changed. Done in the article vault before publishing.

# A highlight across paragraphs is cut at the first paragraph

Open · low severity · failure · newsroom-design-lab

## What we saw

Selecting text that spans two paragraphs and tapping Highlight keeps only the part in the first.

## Why it matters

The reader loses part of what they chose to keep, without being told.

Store highlights as ranges across blocks, or refuse the selection with a message.

# Search results show no snippets

Open · low severity · gap · newsroom-design-lab

## What we saw

The findability prototype searches a 98 KB term index; results are cards with no matching text.

## Why it matters

A reader cannot see why a result matched, so cannot judge it before opening.

## The fix

Snippets from the markdown twins, within a size budget, or computed on a site page rather than in the vault.

# Stacked tables on a phone lose their column labels

Open · low severity · gap · newsroom-design-lab

## What we saw

At 390 px the prototype stacks table rows into blocks without repeating the column names.

## Why it matters

Values without labels on a phone: the reader has to remember what each line means.

## The fix

Repeat the column label in each stacked cell (data-label + ::before).

[Findings](/findings/index.md) / UX-055

# "Ask the article" has never run against a real on-device model

Open · low severity · gap · newsroom-design-lab

## What we saw

The ask view uses Chrome's built-in model when present and a labelled extractive fallback otherwise. Only the fallback and a stub were tested; the model is absent in headless Chrome and likely in the vault frame.

## Why it matters

The feature is shown to readers on a path nobody has seen work.

## The fix

Test in a real Chrome with the model, or use sg.llm with an llm.chat grant; until then say "fallback" in the UI, as it does.

## The record

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Status** | Open |
| **Severity** | Low |
| **Kind** | Gap: something the reader needs is not there |
| **Site** | [newsroom-design-lab](/lab/index.md) |
| **Where** | newsroom-proto-article |
| **Area** | [Article page](/findings/?area=article) |
| **Breaks** | [What a page says about the present is true now](/principles/index.md#state-is-current) |
| **Observed** | 2026-10-11, v0.1.1 |
| **Last checked** | 2026-10-11, v0.1.1 |
| **Source** | [Design lab: what building it measured](/lab/index.md#what-building-the-lab-measured) |
| **Prototype** | [Article & reader primitives](/lab/index.md#newsroom-proto-article), route `ask`, in three directions |

Previous: [UX-054 Stacked tables on a phone lose their column labels](/findings/UX-054.md)

# Findings

Every UX failure and gap in the register, open first, then by severity. A **failure** works against the reader; a **gap** is something the reader needs that is not there. Each status says when it was last checked, and on which version: nothing here claims to be current beyond that.

| ID | Status | Severity | Kind | Site | Area | Finding |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [UX-001](/findings/UX-001.md) | Open | high | failure | newsroom.sgit.ai | First visit | The first phone screen explains how the site is built, not what it is about |
| [UX-002](/findings/UX-002.md) | Open | high | failure | newsroom.sgit.ai | First visit | The home page is 59 phone screens long, with 845 links |
| [UX-024](/findings/UX-024.md) | Open | high | failure | newsroom.sgit.ai | Feedback | All three rating scales start on 3 |
| [UX-025](/findings/UX-025.md) | Open | high | gap | newsroom.sgit.ai | Feedback | Ratings never reach the author |
| [UX-028](/findings/UX-028.md) | Open | high | failure | newsroom.sgit.ai | Money | The £5.00 balance chip has no label |
| [UX-029](/findings/UX-029.md) | Open | high | failure | newsroom.sgit.ai | Money | Opening an article charges a penny with no notice |
| [UX-032](/findings/UX-032.md) | Open | high | gap | newsroom.sgit.ai | Trust | Nothing shows real money moving |
| [UX-033](/findings/UX-033.md) | Open | high | gap | newsroom.sgit.ai | Trust | It is unclear how a writer gets paid |
| [UX-034](/findings/UX-034.md) | Open | high | gap | newsroom.sgit.ai | Trust | No contact for a pilot on the Replicate page |
| [UX-037](/findings/UX-037.md) | Open | high | failure | newsroom.sgit.ai | Consistency | Two domains claim to be canonical for the same article |
| [UX-044](/findings/UX-044.md) | Open | high | failure | newsroom.sgit.ai | Personas | The founder page says "the picks above" and no picks render on a phone |
| [UX-046](/findings/UX-046.md) | Open | high | failure | dev.vault.sgraph.ai | Platform | Setting location.hash inside a vault app re-navigates the frame: every link silently dead |
| [UX-003](/findings/UX-003.md) | Open | medium | gap | newsroom.sgit.ai | First visit | The masthead line describes a method, not a subject |

## How a finding gets here

Someone uses the site as a stranger would: a phone, a link, three minutes. What gets in their way is written down with the evidence, the date and the version, then named against a [principle](/principles/index.md). The [method](/method/index.md) has the details. The first source was the [newsroom UX review of 11 October 2026](/reviews/newsroom-2026-10-11.md); new findings come from the same kind of look at any site in the network.

This site follows its own principles, or it is a finding too: the first screen says what it is, every view is a link, every count is generated from [one file](/data/findings.json), and the content is there without JavaScript.


==============================================================================
/lab/  ·  /lab/index.md
==============================================================================

# The Newsroom Design Lab

A finding says what is wrong. The lab shows what right could look like. Built 11 to 13 October 2026, it is four [SGit vaults](https://sgit.ai/), each a self-contained app, that try the fixes from the [newsroom review](/reviews/newsroom-2026-10-11.md) on the real newsroom data (a byte-faithful snapshot of 73 articles), **in three design directions each**, so that a direction can be chosen by looking rather than by arguing. Nothing in the lab changes the live site.

Every view in the lab says which step of the reader's path it moves them to: **arrive** through a link someone sent, **read** and rate, **come back**, **ask**, **act**.

## Three directions

A direction is a different design, not a recolour: different hierarchy, type, density and interaction, over the same data. Every vault has a switch in its top bar, and a Compare view that shows all three at phone width.

| Direction | The idea | Looks like |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **A · Broadsheet** | A serious publication. Editorial hierarchy, one lead, a named author with a stated purpose. | Serif headlines, warm paper, rules between columns, kickers, restrained colour. FT / Guardian long-read feel. |
| **B · Briefing** | Answers first. Every unit opens with the news in two sentences, then labelled blocks: the news, our view, the evidence, room for disagreement. | Sans, compact cards with reading time and format, bold labels, one accent colour. Semafor / Axios feel. |
| **C · Your desk** | The reader's own newsroom. The persona is the front page; the board, highlights, notes and questions are first-class. | App-like: left rail, side column, chips and progress. Readwise / Arc feel. |

## The same screen, three ways

Screenshots at phone width (390 px) from the published vaults, rendered from their own snapshot with the network off. Tap one for the full page.
